Safe resource caps and level conditions apply to seasonal migration.

Construction effective time follows Effective Time = Base Time / (1 + Sum of Speed Bonuses%).

Gathering speed scales with Pioneer crew bonuses and personal logistics research.
Champions come in Epic and Legendary rarities; Legendary Champions are harder to obtain.
Galactic events are stated to run on predictable calendar cycles.

Prince Assistance provides +10% construction speed for 24 hours.

Upgrading shipyards unlocks higher ship tiers including T2 and T3.
The headquarters is described in-game as a trader flagship capable of hyperspace jumps.
Personal Research Lab technologies provide permanent personal attribute upgrades.
Gathering fleets can be deployed to planetary resource nodes.

Shipyards construct escort combat craft.
A Flagship can change Style by replacing its Core Components.
Players can form Commerce Guilds with other players.

Fully depleting a resource node allows a fresh node to spawn in the system.

The game describes cults and space pirates as threats encountered during exploration.

The game describes mind-controlling entities seeking to overturn the galaxy's balance.
Fully depleting a resource node grants a completion bonus.
Champions are also used in ground combat during landing battles and Prime Radiant stages.
Champions serve as commanders in Space Combat and provide fleet attribute bonuses and abilities.
The Flagship Style determines the fleet Style.
Resources below the Warehouse Safe Capacity threshold are 100% immune to enemy looting.

Event milestone rewards can include Legendary hero shards and exclusive flagship blueprints.
Players can build trade networks across different planets.
Seasonal kingdom migration allows players and guilds to relocate to new realms.
The game describes covert maneuvers on Terminus as part of its setting.
Migration rules are presented as supporting competitive balance across galaxy server clusters.
The game describes political conspiracies driven by clone bloodlines on Trantor.

The maximum number of fleets that can be deployed increases as Energy Core level increases.
The Research Lab provides 17 personal battle technologies across 6 tiers.
Style Advantage deals 5% more damage to units with Style disadvantage.
Cross-server Dominion Warzones are part of the inter-server warfare framework shown in the screenshot.
The source recommends prioritizing Fleet Capacity and Shipyard Speed early in progression.

Activating Prince Assistance before major upgrades is recommended for time savings.
Ascendancy Shrines are protected by elite robotic defenders and primary radiation shields.
The daily checklist includes capping 20 guild help assists.
The game states that player decisions can tip the balance of power in the galaxy.
Commerce Guild members can assist each other to reduce construction and research times.
Damage Reduction reduces all damage received.
Fleets with Minor Damage can be immediately recovered after leaving battle without consuming Repair Modules.
Jump Points are formed by Jump Anchors and Jump Relay Stations, usually appearing in pairs to create hyperspace pathways between Star Systems.
After being destroyed by other traders 2 times, a fleet gains Interstellar Shelter for 3 hours.
Each trader can hold only one Overlord title at a time.
Fleet Rating reflects the combat capability of a fleet and is calculated from deployed Flagship, Combat Craft, Champions, Technologies, Heroic Crew Members, and certain Buildings.
Occupying a Port provides continuous resource dividends and attribute bonuses for Guild members.
Actively attacking another trader puts all participating fleets into War Frenzy for 5 minutes.
HP is Maximum Health; reaching 0 means defeat.
Overlords receive exclusive benefits including increased Fleet Attack and a special Overlord emblem.
A Commerce Guild can nominate an Overlord after occupying a Level 4 Star Port in a Border Region or Level 7 Star Port in a Core Region.
While Interstellar Shelter is active, the fleet is immune to attacks from other traders.
The Home Port button on the map can instantly locate the trader’s Home Port.
Energy Core level determines the maximum level of Flagships, Champions, and other buildings.
Monopolized Planet Ports provide continuous resource dividends to all Commerce Guild members.
Combat craft involved in long battles can be destroyed after receiving excessive Major Damage.
Commerce Guild research provides bonuses such as increased Port occupation capacity and ship attribute improvements.
After a fleet is destroyed, it revives at Home Port after a period and gains Rally Up for 2 minutes.
Quick repairs can be performed through the formation list on the left side of the game screen.
There are 6 Overlord seats in Korell Province.
Commerce Guild membership enables events including Defend the Trade Route and Commerce Guild Duel.
Champion Styles are Beam, Kinetic, and Ion.
ATK increases non-INT damage dealt.
A Province is a large administrative division containing multiple Star Systems.
The Power system evaluates overall Power and individual elements based on Energy Core level.
Upon entering Korell, a trader is randomly assigned to one of four Border Regions as their affiliated region.
While Rally Up is active, the fleet is immune to attacks from other traders.
Increasing Power to milestone values can earn rewards and unlock new Power icons.
Fleets with Major Damage require Repair Modules to be repaired after leaving battle.
Fleets must use Jump Points to move between Star Systems.
Detailed Fleet Rating breakdowns can be viewed in the Attribute Formation interface.
Destroyed combat craft cannot be recovered.
War Frenzy attacks apply a 30% Slow effect to the target.
Champion Roles shown in the Encyclopedia are Attack, Defense, Healing, and Support.
Glory earned in Hunting Ground Star Systems counts toward the event ranking.
Monopolized Star Ports provide continuous resource dividends and global benefits to all Commerce Guild members.
Champion abilities activate in Formation deployment order from left to right.
The Border Region has 4 subdivisions, the Core Region has 2 subdivisions, and the Abyss Region has no subdivisions.
A Commerce Guild is an organization formed by traders.
When attacked, a fleet executes a Counterattack.
Home Port recall attempts regenerate every 15 minutes.
Command Points are a Fleet-only attribute.
The side with higher Morale is shown as inflicting additional battle damage in the Encyclopedia example.
In Space Combat, the side with higher Command Points gains extra damage.
Fleet Ratings of both sides can be viewed and compared on a target profile panel.
DEF reduces non-INT damage received.
War Frenzy increases Fleet ATK by 3%.
Damage against a countered Style is increased by 5%.
Higher-level Star Systems are generally closer to the center of their Province and have higher enemy levels and Glory efficiency.
Neutral Ports in the initial Star System or Ports occupied by the trader’s Commerce Guild can be used as Home Ports.
Launching an attack against another trader removes Rally Up.
Normal Attacks generate Energy; when the Energy bar is full, Champions unleash Active Abilities.
Crit Damage is the multiplier applied when a critical hit lands.
Hunting Ground Star Systems contain Energy Bodies, including Dense Energy and Active Energy capable of repairing ships.
Joining a Commerce Guild unlocks resources, buffs, and multiple features.
Major Damage can be repaired through the Formation interface.
The Power system recommends focusing on lower-rated elements to increase Power more efficiently.
Hyperspace Teleport can be used to change a trader’s affiliated region.
Capturing a Planet Port gives control over the entire Planet.
Each trader can settle in and set only one Port as their Home Port.
Champions have Style and Role as two key lineup attributes.
Adjusting Champion deployment order can maximize ability effectiveness.
Home Port level determines Trade Shipping Level.
Crit Rate is the chance to land a critical hit and affects normal attacks only in Space Combat.
Home Port provides a Construction Speed Bonus.
A Planet is a basic physical unit of a Star System controlled and managed by Planet Ports.
Counterattack damage is displayed below Normal Attack Damage.
Damage Bonus increases all damage dealt.
Commerce Guilds can declare war on Ports.
Combat craft with Major Damage can be repaired in the Mothership Repair Cabin.
Launching an attack against another trader resets the Interstellar Shelter accumulated count and removes the effect.
Joining a Commerce Guild unlocks the Rally feature for team battles.
Total Power is displayed in the upper-left corner of the Home Screen.
A Star Port governs its entire Star System; winning its war gives a Commerce Guild monopoly of the Star Port.
Beam counters Kinetic, Kinetic counters Ion, and Ion counters Beam.
The Star System containing a monopolized Star Port is included in the Commerce Guild’s controlled regions.
INT increases INT damage dealt and reduces INT damage received.
Fleets cannot be operated or attacked while jumping.
Player Power is composed of Flagships, Combat Craft, Champions, Technologies, Heroic Crew Members, and Buildings.
The interval between Killstreak kills must not exceed 3 minutes.
Commerce Guild Shop lets members exchange Guild Vouchers for resources and items including Champion Ascendancy Fragments and Training Manuals.
A rally launches automatically once all participants have joined the Rallied Troop.
Champion Star Level determines which Champion abilities can be unlocked or awakened and increases their ability level caps at certain levels.
Friendly fleets within a Commerce Guild controlled region receive combat bonuses and Trade Shipping rewards increase.
When Energy Core power load exceeds 100%, resource-building production efficiency is reduced by 10%.
The first fleet joining a Port Garrison becomes the garrison leader and provides battle buffs.
Low Power Mode is automatically enabled when Water runs out.
If a trader’s Power reaches 20,000,000 or higher, Glory Protection no longer applies when that trader is attacked by other traders.
After an existing Calamity Ship is defeated, another ship may emerge from the wormhole.
Rallies are coordinated attacks led by Commerce Guild members against special objectives including Tribute Vessels and Ports.
Energy Core power load of 0%–100% is Operating Normally; load above 100% is Overloaded.
Attacking Tribute Vessels requires the Commerce Guild to initiate a rally.
Champion Ability Upgrades use Training Manuals to increase ability levels.
Urgent Orders have five qualities: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Epic, and Legendary.
A trading fleet departs from the Home Port and receives basic resource rewards upon reaching the destination Star Port.
A Flagship Component Set bonus activates when the required amount of same-type, same-quality components is equipped.
Technology research is divided into four branches in the Encyclopedia description.
Killstreak requires an online target and at least 30% of the total damage received by the target to be dealt by the attacker.
When attacking a much weaker trader, Glory earned is progressively reduced based on the power gap between Flagships and combat craft.
A Shrine can focus its firepower on one fleet at a time; rotating a low-HP fleet out can cause the Shrine to switch targets.
After leaving combat, a War Frenzy fleet can use Swap Combat Craft.
The Mothership has three Shipyard styles that produce Kinetic, Beam, and Ion combat craft respectively.
A HELP button appears above the Commerce Guild icon when assistance requests are pending.
Trader Commissions refresh daily at 00:00, 06:00, 12:00, and 18:00 UTC and disappear if not completed within 18 hours.
If a garrisoned fleet enters War Frenzy, all fleets garrisoned at the same Port receive the War Frenzy bonus.
Crew Members are divided into roles and can be accessed from the Energy Core on the Mothership.
A fleet in War Frenzy cannot rejoin a rally targeting a trader or garrison for 60 seconds after leaving it.
Calamity Ships emerge in waves from wormholes in designated Star Systems.
Commerce Guild creation requires Energy Core Level 9 and 2,000 Credits according to the Encyclopedia creation screen.
Trade Shipping has Regular Orders and Urgent Orders.
Attacking Ascendancy Minions consumes Action Points, which gradually replenish over time.
Trader Commissions refresh only in the Star System where the Home Port is located.
Research Center upgrades increase research speed, and speedup items can accelerate research.
Commerce Guild members can request assistance for construction or research.
Fleets in Auto-Join mode undergo auto-repair.
Regular Orders provide basic resources such as Metal, Water, and Galactic Coins and are available within the Home Port range.
Rally fleets combine participant attributes, but only the rally initiator’s buffs and Rally Champion abilities are applied.
Deliverer Ark intelligence can be obtained by defeating Ascendancy Minions or completing Deliverer Ark Trader Commissions.
In Single Selection mode, only the selected fleet executes the current Flagship command.
Higher-quality Flagship Components provide greater attribute increases.
When Ascendancy Minions are defeated, participating fleets receive rewards.
Tapping Share sends target information to the Chat channel.
Higher fleet load provides richer Urgent Order rewards.
Completing a certain number of Trader Commissions each day grants Home Port Dividends.
Tribute Vessels must be destroyed in one go or they will be fully repaired by the Ascendancy cultists.
Crew Members can be assigned to Mothership buildings to provide production boosts and abilities.
In Select All mode, all fleets respond to the current Flagship command.
If a trade fleet is defeated, 5% of order rewards exceeding the Warehouse protection limit can be plundered by the attacker.
Increasing Trader Network level immediately refreshes one commission and permanently increases individual commission rewards and commission quality on refresh.
The Echo Hub consists of 10 stages with multiple progress steps and nodes.
Ascendancy Shrines require rallies to defeat them.
Commerce Guild controlled regions expand as the Guild monopolizes Ports.
AI-controlled troops do not fully occupy rally slots.
Champion Star Promotion uses Champion Fragments and increases base attributes.
Higher Home Port level increases the likelihood of receiving higher-quality Trader Commissions.
Higher Urgent Order quality provides richer rewards.
Continuously upgrading a Flagship improves its base attributes and is presented as important for trade routes.
Flagship Promotion uses Blueprints and increases base attributes while unlocking or enhancing Flagship skills.
Auto-Join supported targets include Tribute Vessels, Ports, and Deliverer Arks.
Urgent Orders provide a large amount of items and have a daily acceptance limit that can be raised by Energy Core level.
Advanced combat craft become available when a Shipyard reaches certain levels.
Overclocked Mode doubles Water consumption, greatly increases power generation, and boosts resource-building output by 10%.
Certain Ascendancy-related commissions can be completed even after the corresponding enemy was defeated in another Star System.
Research progression in prerequisite technologies determines the upper limit of current research.
Auto-Join settings can be configured for rally events.
Low Power Mode stops consuming Water but reduces resource-building production efficiency by 20%.
When an Auto-Join rally fleet’s HP drops below 30%, it stops auto-joining rallies.
When a Guild member initiates a rally, a red Flag button appears on the right side of the Home Screen for joining rallies.
Heroic Crew Members can be assigned to one of three Echo Hub Styles, granting combat bonuses and abilities to Champion fleets of the corresponding Style.
Tapping an enemy body or portrait selects it as a target.
Commerce Guild Technology is researched collectively by Guild members.
Technology research is conducted at the Research Center on the Mothership.
Dragging a fleet’s body or icon moves it and can initiate an attack.
Commerce Guild Marks can be placed by Guild administrators to guide members toward objectives.
Enhancing all nodes in an Echo Hub stage allows progression to the next stage and unlocks new bonuses or assignment slots.
The Core Component determines the Flagship Style and the Style of the entire fleet.
While in War Frenzy, fleets cannot teleport, be recalled, or be repaired.
Port Guard increases Fleet DEF by 5% while a fleet is garrisoned at a Port.
Occupying Ports increases Urgent Order rewards.
Star Systems Level 7–9 have 100% Glory Acquisition Efficiency.
Each escort mission passes through 3 trade points and earns phase rewards at each point.
After first occupation, participating victorious Guild members receive Participation Rewards.
Each Arms Race round lasts 30 minutes and contains 5 waves.
During Arms Race, Guild members increase Morale by defeating Tribute Vessels.
Defend the Trade Route requires at least 20 Commerce Guild members to manually start or schedule.
Final Exploration Rewards unlock all unknown areas in a Star System.
Killstreak Effects replace the default broadcast after achieving a Killstreak and accumulating at least 100,000 Glory or equivalent Major Damage.
In Kaboom, Robots!, traders can challenge stages unlimited times per day, while participation rewards can be claimed once per day.
Star Systems Level 4–6 have 50% Glory Acquisition Efficiency.
Star Systems Level 1–3 have 0% Glory Acquisition Efficiency.
Damage dealt by the Cargo Dreadnought is included in total damage statistics for participating traders.
Shadowfront contains 8 Lesser Vaults and 2 Central Vaults.
Players must have been in the Commerce Guild for at least 48 hours to be eligible for Arms Race event rewards.
The War Prism spawns twice during the Battlefield Showdown day.
If an excavation fleet is defeated during the process, a portion of the ruin rewards is lost.
A War Prism remains for 30 minutes after spawning and disappears if not destroyed.
Investment attempts have a daily limit that can be raised by upgrading the Energy Core.
Ruin excavation requires fleets to garrison the ruins.
Arms Race is a Commerce Guild event started or scheduled by Guild administrators.
Arms Race individual rewards are based on the highest individual damage in a single stage.
Defeated fleets inside the Battlefield Star System revive at the Teleport Spot; fleets defeated outside revive at Home Port.
Defend the Trade Route has a 3-minute preparation period before escort fleets can be dispatched.
Bots defeated in each Kaboom, Robots! stage count toward the event leaderboard.
Joining a Guild-admin rally during Arms Race grants an additional 15% damage bonus against Drill Cruisers.
Glory Acquisition Efficiency is applied as a multiplier when calculating final Glory rewards.
Only after a Star Port is available can the Commerce Guild Chairman and eligible officers declare war on it.
Traders inside the Outer Rim Outpost Shadowfront cannot be attacked by other Commerce Guilds.
Arms Race Stage A locks the current Morale Level; Stage B can be activated within 24 hours after Stage A ends and inherits Stage A Morale Level and difficulty.
Commerce Guild Duel Battlefield Showdown designates a specific Star System as the battlefield on the final day.
Ascendancy fleets attempt to block the Cargo Dreadnought during each escort phase.
Water is used for Mothership facility upgrades, combat craft manufacturing, and Technology research.
Non-Guild members’ trade orders can be hacked to steal a random item from their order rewards.
Arms Race Guild rewards are distributed based on combined damage from both stages.
Kaboom, Robots! achievement rewards are based on the number of bots defeated.
Landing the last hit on a War Prism grants a large amount of points to the attacking Guild.
War Prisms spawn after the duel begins and both Guilds earn points by damaging them.
Metal is used for Mothership facility upgrades, combat craft manufacturing, and Technology research.
After a Commerce Guild occupies a Star Port, members’ fleets can receive combat buffs within the Star System through Stellar Aura.
During the Commerce Guild Duel Battlefield Showdown, Glory can be converted to points and attacking opposing Guild members acquires Glory at a rate of 150%.
Exploration Progress is earned by scanning unknown planets, experiencing space events, and completing planetary missions.
Escort fleets increase the Cargo Dreadnought’s HP.
After a Commerce Guild occupies a Planet Port, members can settle there and make it their Traders’ Home Port.
After the declaration countdown ends, Commerce Guilds must launch an attack on the target Port.
After first occupation, all members of the victorious Commerce Guild share in Honor Rewards.
Ruin quality improves with Energy Core level.
Exploration Progress is tracked for each Star System.
Guild members can invest in other Guild members’ orders to receive a random item from the order after a waiting period.
Other traders can plunder ruins being excavated by another trader.
The Port garrison must be defeated before the Commerce Guild can occupy the Port.
Defend the Trade Route can be manually started or scheduled by the Chairman and officers of Level 4 or higher.
Defend the Trade Route concludes when its timer ends regardless of whether the Cargo Dreadnought reaches the final trade point or is destroyed.
Only Urgent Orders can be hacked.
F2P players are advised to save resources for Top 100 and GvG after Project: Daybreak and Vault Trials.
Counsellor of Internal Affairs is reported to provide +50% Water, +50% Metal, and +10% Trade Fleet Speed at action start.
GvG is generally prioritized over Top 100 on new servers for long-term progression rewards.
Research Counsellor is reported to provide +20% Research Speed and +10% Building Speed at action start.
Construction Counsellor is reported to provide +20% Building Speed and +10% Research Speed at action start.
Military Counsellor is reported to provide +20% Combat Manufacturing and +5% Major Damage Resistance at action start.
Community advice warns players to wait to spend Prismatic Cores until Legendary components are available.
Community testing recommends Jodie/Lily/Ajita as an Ion team, with Kama for Lily and Phade for Ajita as reported replacements.
Community reports that event items explicitly marked as reclaimed after an event should be used before the event ends or they will be lost.
Whether raising both Space and Ground skills for an unused hero is worthwhile remains unanswered in the supplied Discord data.
Community reports that Novice Protection ends when upgrading from Core 9 to Core 10, after which the player can be attacked even while AFK.
A player-made Canva territory planning map is used by some community members to visualize planets and coordinate territory changes.
Community advice says to spend rather than hoard resources specifically around major events such as Top 100 and GvG.
Community players identify the Strikeback pack as one of the stronger ROI purchases.
Strategic Counsellor is reported to provide +5% Enemy Major Damage Rate and +20% Repair Module Production at action start.
Community reports that title buffs must be active when an action starts to affect that action, and the buff continues after the title is removed.
Community reports that under the Core 9→10 Novice Protection transition, resources remain protected and the player cannot be fully zeroed, while small fleet ships may still be lost.
On established servers, community players are divided between prioritizing Top 100 for immediate resources and prioritizing GvG for overall rewards.
Home Port repairing damaged fleets remains an unanswered community question in the supplied Discord data.
Community reports that the Trader Prince/CFO position must be retained for the full trade duration to receive the full trade benefit.
Community advice says regular purchase packs generally have poor ROI for F2P players.
Community advice is to stay in a planetary system displaying 0% Glory because attackers receive no Glory from hitting the player; players explicitly note this is not guaranteed safety.
Acting Prince is reported by the community to provide +12.5% Building Speed, +12.5% Research Speed, and +12.5% Combat Manufacturing at action start.
Community testing recommends Klara/Lucius/Doug as a Beam team, with Aliya for Klara and Evan for Lucius as reported replacements.
Community advice for players leaving Novice Protection is to use guild-controlled territory and garrison when possible.

Community testing recommends Eva/Zora/Killer Bee as a Kinetic team, with Lani as a reported replacement for Eva or Zora, Riian as a Zora replacement if Lani is already used, and Cocoon as a Killer Bee replacement.
Community advice says first-purchase rewards at each purchase tier can be worthwhile, while repeated purchases are generally considered less valuable.
